proposals.before: Seeing his integrity and learning he still owned no house, the emperor ordered fifty rooms built for him.
proposals.after: Seeing that Zhi was pure, loyal, and upright in conduct and had never owned a house, the emperor ordered fifty rooms built for him.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic 'learning' does not render 履正 ('walking uprightly'); the Chinese praises purity, loyalty, and correct conduct, not scholarship.

proposals.before: Emperor Ming of Wei granted this; an edict was still issued praising him, encouraging him with the fine example of Huang Ba, and he was promoted to General Who Suppresses Brigands.
proposals.after: Emperor Ming of Wei granted this; an edict was still issued praising him, encouraging him with the fine example of Huang Ba, and he was additionally granted the title General Who Suppresses Brigands.
proposals.reason: 加 marks an added concurrent title, not a replacement promotion; the idiomatic already has 'added the title'.

proposals.before: The court mourned him, enriched his grave goods, gave the posthumous name Zhen ('steadfast'), and allotted one hundred mu of burial land.
proposals.after: The emperor held mourning for him, burial gifts were given beyond the norm, his posthumous name was Zhen ('steadfast'), and he was granted a burial plot of one hundred mu.
proposals.reason: Chinese 帝為舉哀 makes the emperor the mourner; 'the court' shifts the agent.

proposals.before: Wei once remonstrated that current policy was too lenient; the emperor said: 'Below the Masters of Writing supervisors, I grant no indulgence.'
proposals.after: Wei once remonstrated that current policy was too lenient; the emperor said: 'Below the gentlemen of the Masters of Writing, I grant no indulgence.'
proposals.reason: 尚書郎 is the gentlemen of the Masters of Writing, not 'supervisors'; the emperor is drawing the line below that grade.

proposals.before: Later promoted Administrator of Xiangdong, he served as palace gentleman to Prince Chengdu Sima Ying; died of illness.
proposals.after: Later promoted Administrator of Xiangdong, he served as Chamberlain of the Palace Attendants (langzhongling) to Prince Chengdu Sima Ying; died of illness.
proposals.reason: 郎中令 is the chamberlain of palace attendants, not an ordinary palace gentleman; the idiomatic rendering already has the higher office.

proposals.before: Under Wei he entered the central ministries, rose to gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and served as palace attendant.
proposals.after: Under Wei he was summoned to a ducal office, rose by steps to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and served as Supervising Secretary.
proposals.reason: 辟公府 is summons to a Three-Ducal office, not entry into the central ministries; 給事中 is Supervising Secretary/palace attendant in the successive-post sense already in the literal.

proposals.before: Soon he commanded the guards, ran Henan, and took the granaries ministry—but the humane magistrate was gone; he turned petty and cruel.
proposals.after: Soon he was promoted Commandant of the Guards, Intendant of Henan, and Minister of Agriculture, but he no longer had a reputation for capability and became harsh and fussy.
proposals.reason: 無復能名 means he no longer had a reputation for ability, not that a humane magistrate had disappeared.

proposals.before: The prefect had Pan Jing draft the proper notice; Luoyang adopted it as precedent.
proposals.after: He then had Jing compose a text and sent him to the capital, taking it as the permanent precedent.
proposals.reason: The Chinese sends Jing to 京師 with a composed text as 永式; it does not name Luoyang or call the piece a 'proper notice'.

proposals.before: His elder sister had married into the Sun clan and died early, leaving a grandson Mai; Guang carried him south in flight; though bandits pressed hard, he never abandoned the child.
proposals.after: His elder sister had married into the Sun clan and died early, leaving a son named Mai; Guang carried him south in flight; though bandits pressed hard, he never abandoned the child.
proposals.reason: After 適孫氏, 有孫名邁 is the sister's child Sun Mai (the nephew Guang carried), not a further grandson.

proposals.before: Rated ‘brilliant’ second grade, he taught literature for Prince Wu, tutored the heir, and joined Prince Donghai Sima Yue's staff.
proposals.after: Rated ‘brilliant’ second grade, he became literary instructor to the Prince of Wu, then served in succession as Foreman Clerk of the Heir Apparent (xianma) and as adjutant to Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai.
proposals.reason: 太子洗馬 is a specific court office, not generic tutoring of the heir; 曆 marks a sequence of posts.

proposals.before: Huan Yi and Yu Wei inspected the hungry, then impeached him for opening stores.
proposals.after: The court sent Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary Huan Yi, together with Yu, to comfort the starving and see whether affairs stood well, then impeached You for issuing grain without authorization.
proposals.reason: 虞慰勞 is the surname Yu plus the verb 'to comfort'; 慰 is not part of the personal name.

proposals.before: In the second year of Taining, Mingdi plotted against Wang Dun by moving Deng You to Kuaiji.
proposals.after: In the second year of Taining, when Wang Dun rebelled, Emperor Ming secretly planned to raise troops and thereupon transferred You to Administrator of Kuaiji.
proposals.reason: The Chinese sequences Wang Dun's revolt, Mingdi's secret plan to raise troops, and the Kuaiji transfer; it does not say the transfer itself was the plot against Wang Dun.

proposals.before: Wu Yin-zhi (courtesy Chumo) of Juancheng descended six generations from Wei attendant Wu Zhi.
proposals.after: Wu Yin-zhi (courtesy Chumo), a man of Juancheng in Puyang, was a sixth-generation descendant of Wei attendant Wu Zhi.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits 濮陽, which the Chinese and literal both locate as Puyang Juancheng.

proposals.before: He mourned his father so loudly strangers wept.
proposals.after: When he was a little over ten he suffered his father's death; whenever he wailed, passersby wept.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic drops 年十餘, the only age given for the father's death.

proposals.before: Liu Yu demanded his release; months passed before he sailed home.
proposals.after: Liu Yu wrote Xun ordering Yin-zhi returned; only after a long interval did he come back.
proposals.reason: 久方得反 is an unspecified long interval, not 'months'.

proposals.before: Yet Deng You tying his son abandoned kinship—if fate forced choice, why bind the boy to a tree?
proposals.after: Yet You abandoned his son to preserve his nephew, severing affection by righteousness—if strength truly failed, one might cut feeling and endure pain—why beforehand bind him with fetters and cut off one who would run to help!
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents a tree, omits 存侄, and fuses 徽纆 (fetters) into the opening clause.

proposals.before: Shiying exhausted fidelity to the house of Cao, forcing gates and breaking barriers; the Emperor Xuan unleashed thunderbolt wrath yet rewarded steadfast martyrdom—is it not that once mastery rested with him, he desired men whose integrity even critics must acknowledge!
proposals.after: Shiying exhausted fidelity to the house of Cao, forcing gates and breaking barriers; Emperor Xuan held back thunderbolt wrath and rewarded steadfast loyalty—is it not that once mastery rested with him, he desired men whose integrity even critics must acknowledge!
proposals.reason: 收雷霆之威 is restraining/withdrawing wrath, not unleashing it; 烈 here is ardent loyalty, not necessarily martyrdom.

decisions.reason: The original 'integrity and learning' misrenders 清忠履正, which praises purity, loyalty, and upright conduct, not scholarship; the replacement matches the Chinese and remains natural English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 帝以芝清忠履正，素無居宅

decisions.reason: 加討寇將軍 marks an additional concurrent title, so 'promoted' overstates a replacement; 'additionally granted the title' is accurate.
帝為舉哀 makes the emperor the mourner; 'the court' wrongly shifts the agent, and the rest of the replacement follows 賵贈有加, 諡曰貞, 賜塋田百畝.
尚書郎 is the gentlemen/lang of the Masters of Writing, not 'supervisors'; Hu Wei's next reply about 丞郎令史 confirms a grade line, not a supervisory office.
郎中令 is the princely chamberlain of palace attendants, not ordinary 郎中 'palace gentleman'; the replacement restores the correct office.
辟公府 is a summons to a ducal office, not entry into the central ministries; 累遷尚書郎 and 曆給事中 are stepwise promotion then Supervising Secretary, which the original 'palace attendant' blurs with 侍中.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 魏時辟公府，累遷尚書郎，曆給事中

decisions.reason: 無復能名 means he no longer had a reputation for ability, not that a humane magistrate vanished; 苛碎 is harsh and fussy, and the office titles match 衛尉、河南尹、大司農.
遂遣京作文，使詣京師，以為永式 has Jing compose a text and go to the capital as a lasting model; the original invents Luoyang and a 'proper notice'.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遂遣京作文，使詣京師，以為永式

decisions.reason: After 姊適孫氏, 有孫名邁 names the sister's son Sun Mai, the nephew Guang carried; reading 孫 as 'grandson' invents an extra generation.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 姊適孫氏，早亡，有孫名邁

decisions.reason: 吳王文學 is the office of literary instructor, 太子洗馬 is Foreman Clerk of the Heir Apparent rather than informal tutoring, and 曆 marks successive posts including 東海王越參軍.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 為吳王文學，曆太子洗馬、東海王越參軍

decisions.reason: 臺遣散騎常侍桓彝、虞慰勞饑人 sends Huan Yi and a man surnamed Yu to comfort the hungry; 慰勞 is the verb 'to comfort', not a given name Wei.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 臺遣散騎常侍桓彝、虞慰勞饑人

decisions.reason: The Chinese sequences 王敦反, then 明帝密謀起兵, then 乃遷攸為會稽太守; the original wrongly treats the Kuaiji transfer as itself the plot against Wang Dun.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 太寧二年，王敦反，明帝密謀起兵，乃遷攸為會稽太守

decisions.reason: 濮陽鄄城人 locates him in Juancheng of Puyang; omitting 濮陽 drops a stated native-place element.
年十餘，丁父憂 dates the father's death to when Yin-zhi was a little over ten; the original drops that age.
劉裕與循書 is a letter ordering return, and 久方得反 is an unspecified long interval, not 'months' or a demand without a letter.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 劉裕與循書，令遣隱之還，久方得反

decisions.reason: 棄子存侄，以義斷恩 and 預加徽纆，絕其奔走 name preserving the nephew and binding with fetters; the original invents a tree and omits the nephew.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 攸棄子存侄，以義斷恩……何至預加徽纆，絕其奔走者乎

decisions.reason: 收雷霆之威 is holding back or withdrawing wrath, not unleashing it; 獎忠貞之烈 rewards ardent loyalty, not martyrdom.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 宣帝收雷霆之威，獎忠貞之烈

claimRetractions.reason: The personal name 'Yu Wei' exists only because idiomatic English fused the verb 慰勞 onto the surname 虞; the source supports only 虞.

work.en: temple notice adopted as permanent precedent
composed text adopted as permanent precedent

claimRevisions.reason: The extracted work title 'temple notice' comes from the bad idiomatic rendering; the Chinese is only 作文 adopted as 永式.
Jing was sent with a composed text, not a 'notice' invented by the translation.

value.action: had Jing compose the temple notice and send it to the capital
had Jing compose a text and send it to the capital

claimRevisions.reason: Zhao Xin's action is having Jing compose a text and send it to the capital, not draft a temple notice.
